representation_a: tracked application.yml selects dev/Oracle but contains no datasource
representation_b: tracked application-mysql.yml and root Compose use MySQL
current_behavior: Actual selected datasource depends on untracked/absent profile configuration
risk: Migration and runtime schema cannot be inferred; accidental environment connection risk
a5_requirement: Define environment-neutral datastore contract and explicit profile/schema compatibility record

representation_a: execution trace Flyway points to classpath:db/migration
representation_b: only tracked trace migration is db/migration-oracle
current_behavior: Visible default location does not contain the Oracle migration
risk: Schema may not initialize under visible configuration
a5_requirement: Bind migration dialect/location/version explicitly and test compatibility

representation_a: Java CDP uses CLOB strings and manual JSON mapping
representation_b: DiagnosisRecord/examination fields declare json while Oracle migration uses CLOB
current_behavior: Serialization and database validation differ by entity/dialect
risk: Invalid JSON and cross-dialect behavior can be silent
a5_requirement: Define source JSON Schema, canonical serialization and database representation mapping

representation_a: CDPManager uses pessimistic lock and server-side version increment
representation_b: Python ToolContext carries reference version but readers/direct writers do not enforce it
current_behavior: Multiple writers can submit broad maps without caller expected-version
risk: Lost intent, stale overwrites and non-replayable ordering
a5_requirement: StatePatch/CommitResult must require expected version, idempotency and conflict result

representation_a: Java entity stores named CLOB aggregates
representation_b: eight Python readers map snake_case/camelCase; services define varied ToolContext/ToolResult shapes
current_behavior: Adapters use arbitrary dict/map fields and silent empty fallbacks
risk: Unmapped fields, type loss and inconsistent clinical state
a5_requirement: A5 schemas must enumerate canonical fields, aliases, optionality and unmapped-field preservation

representation_a: diagnosis-service ExaminationRecord lacks ocr_status and declares indexes
representation_b: examination-service ExaminationRecord adds ocr_status and declares no indexes
current_behavior: Two services map the same table name with different entity definitions
risk: Runtime DDL/update behavior and field visibility can diverge
a5_requirement: One canonical schema plus generated language mappings and explicit ownership

representation_a: Oracle migration has examination_record without ocr_status
representation_b: examination-service visible MySQL config uses hibernate.ddl-auto=update
current_behavior: Hibernate may mutate MySQL while Oracle migration stays unchanged
a5_requirement: A5 records field contract; later migration task owns explicit dialect migrations

representation_b: follow-up, health-state and wellness entities use Long/NUMBER(19)
current_behavior: Patient identity type changes across tables without foreign keys
risk: Cross-record linkage and tenant/patient isolation are unreliable
a5_requirement: Define canonical Patient/Encounter identifier types and compatibility mapping

representation_a: execution_trace relational rows contain input/output/error payloads
representation_b: CDP contains execution_trace CLOB summary and frontend consumes stream DTO variants
current_behavior: Technical trace is stored and projected through multiple clinical/data surfaces
risk: PHI duplication, inconsistent retention and unclear authority
a5_requirement: Separate technical Trace, AgentEvent, ClinicalDecisionRecord and patient-safe delivery contracts

representation_a: Redis SETEX gives 1800-second TTL and persisted Compose volume
representation_b: memory fallback has no TTL or persistence
current_behavior: A Redis error silently changes retention and recovery behavior
risk: Unbounded memory, lost context on restart and cache divergence
a5_requirement: Contract must declare authority, expiry, fallback state and reconciliation behavior

representation_a: schema_service defines 18 labels, 21 relationships, 17 constraints and 9 indexes
representation_b: four importers and validator are TODO and return success with zero rows
current_behavior: Schema APIs can report created structures while imports report success without data
risk: False readiness and unverifiable medical knowledge lineage
a5_requirement: Knowledge contracts require source/version/release/import result and non-zero validation semantics

representation_a: diagnosis path query assumes Symptom/Disease with cui/name
representation_b: management schema emphasizes display_id/uuid and many extra labels
current_behavior: No evidence proves imported nodes satisfy diagnosis query identifiers
risk: Empty-path fallback can hide incompatible graph data
a5_requirement: A5 knowledge references must define stable identifiers; D phase validates graph benefit

representation_b: no Milvus service, client, collection or schema exists
current_behavior: Configuration is present but no executable access path is confirmed
risk: False assumption of vector availability and unknown patient/medical isolation
a5_requirement: A5 defines reference metadata only; ADR/D phase decides implementation and namespace

risk: Concurrent writes, dirty deployments and unaudited release changes
